newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks flat to lower, prices to go down.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks flat to lower, prices to go down.

text.p: Croatian stocks ended steady to lower on Wednesday in dull trade and brokers said prices were likely to slip as market liquidity wears down.
"The end of the year on such small markets is always bad," said Damir Cikotic from Split's Factor brokerage.
"Insolvency will grow so we expect nothing bigger to happen before spring. Trading will be on small volumes, so prices are likely to go down," he said.
Four of eight active issues were flat, three fell and one rose. Volume dropped to 13,120 shares, and stocks turnover was also lower at 8.9 million kuna.
The only gainer Zagrebacka Banka rose 14 kuna to 1,020. It was also the most actively traded issue with 8,381 shares sold. Pliva inched down 2.10 kuna to 13,500, selling only seven shares.
Traders said that only Zagrebacka and drugs firm Pliva, which are sold abroad, should resist the downward trend.
The biggest loser hotelier Arenaturist was down 20 kuna, or 13.3 pct, to 130, on volume of 324 shares. Another loser, hotelier Istraturist, fell five kuna to 190, with 20 units sold.
Three active hoteliers remained flat on Wednesday. Jadranturist traded at 290 kuna on volume of 178 shares, Laguna at 1,150 with 41 units sold, and Suncani Hvar at 61 kuna on volume of 533 shares.
Food processor Podravka was also stable at 225 kuna, selling 744 shares.
The second tranche of public debt refinancing bonds rose to 7.0 from 6.0 percent above par, on turnover of 11 million kuna.
